conclusion.justification: The report explicitly states that the claim is strongly supported by clinical evidence, citing multiple randomized clinical trials, FDA approval, and systematic reviews demonstrating that add-on cannabidiol significantly reduces convulsive seizure frequency in children with Dravet syndrome.
conclusion.label: endorses

report:
The claim that add-on cannabidiol reduces convulsive seizure frequency in children with Dravet syndrome is strongly supported by clinical evidence. A landmark 2017 double-blind, placebo-controlled trial published in the *New England Journal of Medicine* randomized 120 children and young adults with Dravet syndrome to receive cannabidiol (20 mg/kg/day) or placebo alongside standard antiepileptic treatment. Cannabidiol reduced convulsive seizure frequency by 39% from baseline, significantly outperforming placebo. A subsequent dose-ranging randomized clinical trial of 199 children confirmed these findings, showing a 48.7% reduction in convulsive seizures with a 10 mg/kg/day dose. Based on this robust evidence, the FDA approved Epidiolex (cannabidiol) in 2018 for the treatment of seizures associated with Dravet syndrome in patients two years and older. Systematic reviews further corroborate that adjunctive cannabidiol is an effective antiepileptic intervention for this severe, drug-resistant epilepsy syndrome. While generally effective, cannabidiol was associated with higher rates of adverse events compared to placebo.
